title: Monitoring memory
subtitle: RAM, swap, paging, and live vmstat samples

cards.meaning: free -h = how much RAM is left; vmstat = is it swapping / waiting on I/O right now?
cards.notes: Snapshot of amounts vs activity (paging, I/O, CPU)

cards.meaning: Disk overflow for RAM when memory is tight
cards.notes: These tools show how much is used and whether the machine is paging

cards.meaning: Snapshot of RAM and swap with human-readable sizes (M, G)
cards.notes: Shows total / used / free / shared / buff/cache / available

cards.meaning: Installed RAM / configured swap
cards.notes: Capacity lines

cards.meaning: Memory in use (not including reclaimable cache, depending on free version)
cards.notes: Do not panic on used alone — check available

cards.meaning: Completely unused memory
cards.notes: Low free with high buff/cache is often normal on Linux

cards.meaning: tmpfs / shared memory (often small)
cards.notes: Usually not the main capacity signal

cards.meaning: Kernel buffers + page cache — file data kept in RAM; not wasted
cards.notes: Can be given to apps when needed. Linux loves to fill RAM with cache

cards.meaning: Estimate of RAM still usable for new workloads (free + reclaimable cache)
cards.notes: The number to trust — read available, not only free. Cache is a spare tank

cards.meaning: When available is tiny and swap is climbing
cards.notes: Low free + high buff/cache alone is normal

cards.meaning: Reports processes, memory, paging, block I/O, interrupts, and CPU
cards.notes: Can set a sampling interval and watch near real time

cards.meaning: Show active/inactive memory instead of the default buffer/cache split
cards.notes: Snapshot of run/block queues, RAM, swap in/out, I/O, CPU

cards.meaning: Runnable processes (want CPU); high r = CPU queue
cards.notes: Under procs group

cards.meaning: Blocked processes (usually I/O); high b = waiting on disk
cards.notes: Under procs group

cards.meaning: Swap used (KB)
cards.notes: Amount of swap currently in use

cards.meaning: Idle RAM
cards.notes: Completely free memory in the vmstat table

cards.meaning: Inactive vs active pages (shown with -a)
cards.notes: Replaces the default buffer/cache memory split

cards.meaning: Swap in — KB/s read from swap into RAM
cards.notes: Pair with so; sustained activity means RAM pressure

cards.meaning: Swap out — KB/s written from RAM to swap
cards.notes: Sustained so = RAM pressure; si/so > 0 and climbing = thrashing

cards.meaning: Block in / block out — disk KB/s
cards.notes: Block device I/O rates

cards.meaning: Interrupts / context switches per second
cards.notes: System activity rates

cards.front: vmstat → us sy id wa st
cards.meaning: user, system, idle, iowait, steal — same story as mpstat
cards.notes: wa high = I/O; st = hypervisor steal

cards.front: Quiet vmstat sample (r=1, b=0, si=so=0, id=100)
cards.meaning: Quiet machine, not swapping
cards.notes: From the course sample output

cards.meaning: Total number of tasks created (forks) since last boot
cards.notes: Fork count since boot

cards.meaning: Wide columns; sample every 1 second, 3 times (live)
cards.notes: First line is often since-boot; later lines are the live interval — same pattern as vmstat 1 3

cards.meaning: Summary counters dump (total memory, pages swapped, forks, CPU ticks, …)
cards.notes: A dump, not a table

cards.meaning: Live repeating sample every 1 second
cards.notes: Memory hook: vmstat 1 = live
